title: The Holy Congregation in Jerusalem
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In [Berakhot 9b:16](https://www.sefaria.org/Berakhot.9b.16): Rabbi Yose ben Elyakim testified in the name of the Holy Congregation in Jerusalem that whoever juxtaposes the redemption blessing to the prayer, etc. In [Rosh Hashanah 19b:13](https://www.sefaria.org/Rosh_Hashanah.19b.13), Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi testified in their name.[^3]

In [Beitzah 14b](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.14b.15) and [27a](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.27a.8), Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi cites Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi, who cites Rabbi Yose ben Shaul. Rabbi Yose ben Shaul reports in Rabbi’s name that Rabbi spoke in the name of the Holy Congregation in Jerusalem. Hyman suggests they were called this because, from the destruction of Betar onward, no Jew was permitted to enter even the area of Jerusalem; nevertheless the exalted pious ones risked their lives and dwelt secretly in Jerusalem (without doubt they bribed [the authorities] on their behalf), and engaged in Torah and prayer. Therefore they called them the Holy Congregation, since they were exposed to the sword at all times. But they are not connected with the 'Holy Community' as explained in its entry.

notes.text: The cause of the name, secret residence and supposed bribery are Hyman’s own conjecture. This congregation is expressly distinguished from Edah Kedoshah, the “Holy Community.”

The same transmission chain appears in both passages. [Beitzah 14b:15](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.14b.15) concerns linings over mixed fabrics, while [Beitzah 27a:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Beitzah.27a.8) concerns a ruling attributed to Rabbi Shimon and his colleagues. Hyman’s explanation of when and how this group lived is his historical reconstruction.

The Berakhot report concerns joining the blessing of redemption to prayer. In Rosh Hashanah, Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi transmits a ruling on the dates for sanctifying the two months of Adar. Both passages explicitly name the Holy Congregation in Jerusalem.
